scope: Twenty frozen full-source inputs, one fixed model checkpoint, no annotated corners or saved templates. Production and learned policy classified their own target masks, so their mask-error percentages are not directly comparable. Source-group separation is not established motif-family or unknown-pretraining separation.
findings: The learned policy adds the yellow/white cross to the same three shared passes: green/white checker, orange/blue checker and green/gold tree. All seven accepted outputs pass editable checks.
Production emits five crops and the learned policy four. Sixteen learned-policy inputs never reach fitting; ten retain an internal rejected quadrilateral, six do not.

The production flower-cap crop is visibly too large and includes the cap artwork and background. Its template fails at 4.97% target disagreement. The production Santa crop is plausible, but its template fails full checks despite 2.51% disagreement.

Several neural silhouettes are visually useful but are rejected by the semicircular-cap/colour-support model. Other rejections protect against visibly wrong overlap corners; globally loosening support gates is not justified.
Printed decoration, foil reflections, dark seams and same-paper newsprint remain paper-classification problems. The museum case and multiple-heart tree scene also expose wrong-object selection.
The four learned accepted motifs are recognizable, but the green checker and cross retain curved grid/border artifacts; low disagreement does not establish recovery of ideal artwork.
timingScope: CPU offline comparison. Crop and fitting timers are separate; models were inferred first. Two SAM variants were evaluated for every image in the diagnostic, not a measured lazy browser deployment. No browser end-to-end speed claim.
nextStep: Counterfactual fitting of all ten final rejected quadrilaterals to distinguish localization/support rejection from downstream mask/curve problems. Keep separate from automatic success counts.
